source.title: Data augmentation instead of explicit regularization

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares test accuracy with and without explicit regularization, including dropout, alongside data augmentation. It does not isolate dropout in its main comparison, which tests removing weight decay and dropout together.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results for removing weight decay and dropout together, and appendix results for dropout-only combinations. Its discussion of random-label fitting, optimizer effects, and other cited findings is background, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out accuracy with and without dropout, and with weight decay and dropout removed together, directly testing V6. It is not a listed original source; arXiv:1802.07042 is a separate, earlier paper by the same authors.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate, but understates the authors' recommendation: they advocate developing models with data augmentation instead of weight decay and dropout, considering explicit regularization only after other elements are fixed and its hyperparameters can be carefully tuned. They acknowledge that these regularizers can help, while emphasizing their tuning costs and poor transfer across architecture and data-size changes.
record.recipe_differences: Tests data augmentation with and without weight decay and dropout on standard image-classification architectures; does not reproduce the original dropout study's fully connected and convolutional classifier regimes or isolate dropout in the main comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with data set, augmentation scheme, explicit-regularization combination, training-data fraction, and architecture depth. The authors report weaker transfer of explicit-regularization hyperparameters across data and architecture changes.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D reports Frobenius weight norms and notes that norm alone does not explain the architecture-change performance differences.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight norms vary with augmentation and regularization but do not fully explain these accuracy differences; this does not test magnitude-aware sharpness.

record.problems: The authors describe the empirical study as limited to over 300 models, three architectures and three data sets. Hyperparameters were retained from original models rather than retuned for the no-regularization conditions; the heavier augmentation scheme was not optimized. The primary comparison removes weight decay and dropout jointly, so it cannot attribute that result to dropout alone. Some reported aggregate analyses exclude the WRN ImageNet regularized result.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix C, Table 6 reports matched dropout/no-dropout comparisons for WRN and DenseNet on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, across augmentation and weight-decay settings. These additional 24 rows are omitted to keep the extraction focused on the directly discussed All-CNN contrasts and the aggregate main comparison; their outcomes are likewise generally mixed and do not support a general dropout benefit.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting and corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

No fully connected classifiers or dropout-rate sweep establishing excessive-dropout underfitting. Reduced-data experiments remove weight decay and dropout jointly, so they do not isolate dropout's small-training-set exception. Dropout hyperparameters are inherited rather than systematically tuned.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization gaps against competing measures.
No removal of examples selected by memorization.

missing.what: All-CNN matched dropout comparisons without batch normalization: CIFAR-10 no/light/heavier augmentation gives 71.98/90.10/91.48% without dropout versus 87.59/92.01/92.18% with dropout; CIFAR-100 gives 39.03/63.00/71.46% versus 60.96/68.01/68.40%. All have no weight decay.

Reduced-data joint-removal results across 80%, 50%, 10% and 1% training fractions, retaining model, augmentation and batch-normalization conditions. Record absolute accuracies because Section 5.2's aggregate fractions use each recipe's own full-data baseline.
Joint-removal comparisons for shallower and deeper All-CNN on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, especially the augmented conditions where removal consistently improves accuracy.

Disaggregate R1's full-data augmented comparisons so improvements and penalties from joint removal remain visible. For example, DenseNet CIFAR-10 with light augmentation falls from 95.38% to 94.67%, whereas All-CNN CIFAR-100 with heavier augmentation rises from 70.59% to 71.25%.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied Table 6 contains three regularization combinations for All-CNN and WRN, and two for DenseNet; it contains no weight-decay-only condition. The record's claim that 24 additional matched dropout comparisons exist for WRN and DenseNet is incorrect. WRN has dropout-only versus neither comparisons, including normalization variants; DenseNet only has joint-removal comparisons. Those declared omissions are not separately listed as missing. The earlier same-author original source warrants treating this as a related extension rather than independent replication.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or corresponding held-out test accuracy.
All tested architectures are convolutional; there is no fully connected comparison.

Does not test fully connected classifiers or very small training sets as such. The main comparison removes dropout and weight decay together; appendix comparisons include dropout alone and in combination with weight decay. It does not establish that dropout alone improves test error in the stated regimes.
Reports Frobenius weight norms, but does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps against norm- or margin-based measures.

rows.subject: All-CNN, WRN and DenseNet
rows.size_stated: All-CNN: 16 / 12 layers and 9.4 / 1.3 M parameters; WRN-28-10: 28 layers, 36.5 M parameters; DenseNet-BC: 101 layers, 0.8 M parameters
rows.operation_detail: Compared training with data augmentation alone against training with the same augmentation plus weight decay and dropout.
rows.measure: Relative test-accuracy improvement over bare-bone baseline
rows.baseline: Adding both augmentation and explicit regularization: average improvement 7.90 %
rows.value: Adding augmentation alone: average improvement 8.57 %; better in 9/16 cases
rows.uncertainty: Difference positive with 95 % confidence; P value = 0.0220
rows.note: Study reports the aggregate comparison across architectures and data sets; the WRN ImageNet regularized result (-6.22 %) was excluded from the average and bootstrap analysis.
rows.check: The aggregate supports V6's qualified joint-removal clause: augmentation alone outperformed augmentation plus both regularizers in 9/16 comparisons. This does not isolate dropout. The reported improvements use (accuracy − baseline)/accuracy × 100, rather than baseline as denominator.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, Figures 2–3 and Table 2: 8.57% versus 7.90% average relative improvement; augmentation alone better in 9/16 cases; bootstrap P = 0.0220.
